explanation: Understanding x86-64 assembly language is crucial for systems programming because it allows direct manipulation of hardware resources and optimization at the lowest level.  This provides insight into how high-level languages interact with the underlying architecture, enabling better performance tuning and debugging of system-level code. It also reveals the intricacies of memory management and processor operations, critical for writing efficient and secure systems software.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
.text
    # Standard SysV ABI (Function Call)
.globl my_func
my_func:
    # Arguments: RDI (arg1), RSI (arg2)
    # Return value: RAX
    mov rax, rdi        # Move arg1 to result register
    add rax, rsi        # Add arg2 (RAX = arg1 + arg2)

    # Use IMUL for signed multiplication
    mov rdx, 8
    imul rdx            # RDX:RAX = RAX * RDX

    ret

.text
    # Addressing Modes (Load/Store)
.data
my_array: .quad 1, 2, 3, 4 # Array of Qwords (8 bytes each)

.text
    mov rdi, my_array   # Base address RDI
    
    # Load 4th element (Index 3 * size 8)
    mov rax, [rdi + 3*8] 

    # Load 4 bytes (Doubleword)
    movzx rbx, BYTE [rdi] # Zero-extend byte load
    
    # Store Qword at [Base + Index*Scale + Displacement]
    mov rcx, 5          # Index
    mov rsi, 0xDEADBEEF
    mov [rdi + rcx*8 + 16], rsi 


.text
    # Control Flow and Flags (CF, ZF, SF, OF)
    mov rax, 10
    mov rbx, 5
    
    cmp rax, rbx        # Compare RAX and RBX (Sets Flags)
    
    je  equal_label     # Jump if Equal (ZF=1)
    jl  less_label      # Jump if Less (Signed comparison)
    ja  greater_label   # Jump if Above (Unsigned comparison)

    jmp end_label

greater_label:
    mov rdx, 1          # True branch
    
end_label:
    nop


.text
    # Stack Frame Setup (Prolog/Epilog)
.globl my_frame_func
my_frame_func:
    push rbp            # Save old base pointer
    mov rbp, rsp        # Establish new frame base

    push r12            # Save callee-saved register
    sub rsp, 48         # Allocate local variables (48 bytes)

    # ... Function Body ...

    mov rax, [rbp - 8]  # Access local variable
    
    add rsp, 48         # Deallocate stack space
    pop r12             # Restore callee-saved register
    
    leave               # mov rsp, rbp; pop rbp
    ret
keywords: x86-64 assembly, systems programming, low-level optimization, assembly language
